resources.string: Your app is just your window in. Like an email app, you can switch it or get a new phone — your conversations don’t live in the app.
The app connects to your provider — your home on the network. You choose who runs it, like picking an email provider, or a regional one such as Datanauten in Berlin.
Everyone picks their own provider. Bob is on matrix.org, Carol on a regional server. No single company owns the network.
The providers talk to each other — this is called federation — just like email flows between different providers. Whoever you pick, you can reach everyone.
A message to Bob hops from your provider to his — sealed so only the two of you can read it — then arrives in his app.
A group room can hold people from many providers at once. Everyone keeps their own home; the conversation is shared across all of them.
